1 │ # Errors from dependency groups and metadata break when they are copied
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ Two of the errors this library raises keep useful details inside them. The cyclic dependency group error keeps the group that was asked for, the group it was found in, and the group it pointed to. The invalid metadata error keeps the name of the field that was wrong. But when one of these errors is saved away and read back — for example written to a file, sent to another program, or stored in a cache — the saved copy cannot be turned back into the same error. The details are dropped and reloading fails.
   6 │ 
   7 │ ## What should happen
   8 │ 
   9 │ A person who saves one of these errors and reads it back should get the same error again. The group names and the field name should still be there, and the message should read exactly the same as before. This should work the same way for both errors.
  10 │ 
  11 │ ## About this project
  12 │ 
  13 │ This project is a library that helps other tools read and check information about Python packages. It knows how to read package version numbers, requirements, dependency groups, and package metadata, and it tells the caller when something is wrong by raising errors. People building packaging tools use it so they do not have to write all of that checking themselves.
  14 │ 
  15 │ ## Problem this solves
  16 │ 
  17 │ When an error is passed between programs or kept for later, it has to survive being copied. Today it does not, so people lose the reason the error happened and cannot show the original message or the group and field details to whoever needs them. This makes it hard to log errors properly or hand them from a worker to the main program.
  18 │ 
  19 │ ## What changed
  20 │ 
  21 │ Both errors now come back whole after being saved and read again. The cyclic dependency group error keeps its three group names, and the invalid metadata error keeps the field name it was raised for. The messages stay the same. Two new checks were added, one for each error, that save the error out, read it back, and compare the details and the message.
  22 │ 
  23 │ ## Impact
  24 │ 
  25 │ Correctness and ease of use when errors are copied.
  26 │ 
  27 │ ## User experience
  28 │ 
  29 │ Before: a person catches the cyclic dependency group error, saves it, reads it back, and the restored error no longer knows which groups were involved, so they cannot re-show the original message. After: they do the same thing and the restored error has the same three group names and the same message as the one they caught. The same holds for the invalid metadata error and its field name.
  30 │ 
  31 │ ## Hints
  32 │ 
  33 │ - /workspace/src/packaging/dependency_groups.py
  34 │ - /workspace/src/packaging/metadata.py

  36 │ class CyclicDependencyGroup(ValueError):
  37 │     """
  38 │     The dependency group includes form a cycle.
  39 │ 
  40 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  41 │     """
  42 │ 
  43 │     def __init__(self, requested_group: str, group: str, include_group: str) -> None:
  44 │         self.requested_group = requested_group
  45 │         self.group = group
  46 │         self.include_group = include_group
  47 │ 
  48 │         if include_group == group:
  49 │             reason = f"{group} includes itself"
  50 │         else:
  51 │             reason = f"{include_group} -> {group}, {group} -> {include_group}"
  52 │         super().__init__(
  53 │             "Cyclic dependency group include while resolving "
  54 │             f"{requested_group}: {reason}"
  55 │         )

  57 │ 
  58 │ # in the PEP 735 spec, the tables in dependency group lists were described as
  59 │ # "Dependency Object Specifiers", but the only defined type of object was a
  60 │ # "Dependency Group Include" -- hence the naming of this error as "Object"
  61 │ class InvalidDependencyGroupObject(ValueError):
  62 │     """
  63 │     A member of a dependency group was identified as a dict, but was not in a valid
  64 │     format.

  66 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  67 │     """
  68 │ 
  69 │

  71 │ # Object Model & Interface
  72 │ # ------------------------
  73 │ 
  74 │ 
  75 │ class DependencyGroupInclude:
  76 │     """
  77 │     A reference to another dependency group by name.
  78 │ 
  79 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  80 │     """
  81 │ 
  82 │     __slots__ = ("include_group",)
  83 │ 
  84 │     def __init__(self, include_group: str) -> None:
  85 │         """
  86 │         Initialize a DependencyGroupInclude.
  87 │ 
  88 │         :param include_group: The name of the group referred to by this include.
  89 │         """
  90 │         self.include_group = include_group
  91 │ 
  92 │     def __repr__(self) -> str:
  93 │         return f"{self.__class__.__name__}({self.include_group!r})"

  96 │ class DependencyGroupResolver:
  97 │     """
  98 │     A resolver for Dependency Group data.
  99 │ 
 100 │     This class handles caching, name normalization, cycle detection, and other
 101 │     parsing requirements. There are only two public methods for exploring the data:
 102 │     ``lookup()`` and ``resolve()``.
 103 │ 
 104 │     :param dependency_groups: A mapping, as provided via pyproject
 105 │         ``[dependency-groups]``.
 106 │ 
 107 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 108 │     """
 109 │ 
 110 │     def __init__(
 111 │         self,
 112 │         dependency_groups: Mapping[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]],
 113 │     ) -> None:
 114 │         errors = _ErrorCollector()
 115 │ 
 116 │         self.dependency_groups = _normalize_group_names(dependency_groups, errors)
 117 │ 
 118 │         # a map of group names to parsed data
 119 │         self._parsed_groups: dict[
 120 │             str, tuple[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude, ...]
 121 │         ] = {}
 122 │         # a map of group names to their ancestors, used for cycle detection
 123 │         self._include_graph_ancestors: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
 124 │         # a cache of completed resolutions to Requirement lists
 125 │         self._resolve_cache: dict[str, tuple[Requirement, ...]] = {}
 126 │ 
 127 │         errors.finalize("[dependency-groups] data was invalid")
 128 │ 
 129 │     def lookup(self, group: str) -> tuple[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude, ...]:
 130 │         """
 131 │         Lookup a group name, returning the parsed dependency data for that group.
 132 │         This will not resolve includes.
 133 │ 
 134 │         :param group: the name of the group to lookup
 135 │         """
 136 │         group = _normalize_name(group)
 137 │ 
 138 │         with _ErrorCollector().on_exit(
 139 │             f"[dependency-groups] data for {group!r} was malformed"
 140 │         ) as errors:
 141 │             return self._parse_group(group, errors)
 142 │ 
 143 │     def resolve(self, group: str) -> tuple[Requirement, ...]:
 144 │         """
 145 │         Resolve a dependency group to a list of requirements.
 146 │ 
 147 │         :param group: the name of the group to resolve
 148 │         """
 149 │         group = _normalize_name(group)
 150 │ 
 151 │         with _ErrorCollector().on_exit(
 152 │             f"[dependency-groups] data for {group!r} was malformed"
 153 │         ) as errors:
 154 │             return self._resolve(group, group, errors)
 155 │ 
 156 │     def _resolve(
 157 │         self, group: str, requested_group: str, errors: _ErrorCollector
 158 │     ) -> tuple[Requirement, ...]:
 159 │         """
 160 │         This is a helper for cached resolution to strings. It preserves the name of the
 161 │         group which the user initially requested in order to present a clearer error in
 162 │         the event that a cycle is detected.
 163 │ 
 164 │         :param group: The normalized name of the group to resolve.
 165 │         :param requested_group: The group which was used in the original, user-facing
 166 │             request.
 167 │         """
 168 │         if group in self._resolve_cache:
 169 │             return self._resolve_cache[group]
 170 │ 
 171 │         parsed = self._parse_group(group, errors)
 172 │ 
 173 │         resolved_group = []
 174 │ 
 175 │         for item in parsed:
 176 │             if isinstance(item, Requirement):
 177 │                 resolved_group.append(item)
 178 │             elif isinstance(item, DependencyGroupInclude):
 179 │                 include_group = _normalize_name(item.include_group)
 180 │ 
 181 │                 # if a group is cyclic, record the error
 182 │                 # otherwise, follow the include_group reference
 183 │                 #
 184 │                 # this allows us to examine all includes in a group, even in the
 185 │                 # presence of errors
 186 │                 if include_group in self._include_graph_ancestors.get(group, ()):
 187 │                     errors.error(
 188 │                         CyclicDependencyGroup(
 189 │                             requested_group, group, item.include_group
 190 │                         )
 191 │                     )
 192 │                 else:
 193 │                     self._include_graph_ancestors[include_group] = (
 194 │                         *self._include_graph_ancestors.get(group, ()),
 195 │                         group,
 196 │                     )
 197 │                     resolved_group.extend(
 198 │                         self._resolve(include_group, requested_group, errors)
 199 │                     )
 200 │             else:  # pragma: no cover
 201 │                 raise NotImplementedError(
 202 │                     f"Invalid dependency group item after parse: {item}"
 203 │                 )
 204 │ 
 205 │         # in the event that errors were detected, present the group as empty and do not
 206 │         # cache the result
 207 │         # this ensures that repeated access to a cyclic group will raise multiple errors
 208 │         if errors.errors:
 209 │             return ()
 210 │ 
 211 │         self._resolve_cache[group] = tuple(resolved_group)
 212 │         return self._resolve_cache[group]
 213 │ 
 214 │     def _parse_group(
 215 │         self, group: str, errors: _ErrorCollector
 216 │     ) -> tuple[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude, ...]:
 217 │         # short circuit -- never do the work twice
 218 │         if group in self._parsed_groups:
 219 │             return self._parsed_groups[group]
 220 │ 
 221 │         if group not in self.dependency_groups:
 222 │             errors.error(LookupError(f"Dependency group '{group}' not found"))
 223 │             return ()
 224 │ 
 225 │         raw_group = self.dependency_groups[group]
 226 │         if isinstance(raw_group, str):
 227 │             errors.error(
 228 │                 TypeError(
 229 │                     f"Dependency group {group!r} contained a string rather than a list."
 230 │                 )
 231 │             )
 232 │             return ()
 233 │ 
 234 │         if not isinstance(raw_group, Sequence):
 235 │             errors.error(
 236 │                 TypeError(f"Dependency group {group!r} is not a sequence type.")
 237 │             )
 238 │             return ()
 239 │ 
 240 │         elements: list[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude] = []
 241 │         for item in raw_group:
 242 │             if isinstance(item, str):
 243 │                 # packaging.requirements.Requirement parsing ensures that this is a
 244 │                 # valid PEP 508 Dependency Specifier. Collect InvalidRequirement
 245 │                 # if it throws that.
 246 │                 with errors.collect(InvalidRequirement):
 247 │                     elements.append(Requirement(item))
 248 │             elif isinstance(item, Mapping):
 249 │                 if tuple(item.keys()) != ("include-group",):
 250 │                     errors.error(
 251 │                         InvalidDependencyGroupObject(
 252 │                             f"Invalid dependency group item: {item!r}"
 253 │                         )
 254 │                     )
 255 │                 else:
 256 │                     include_group = item["include-group"]
 257 │                     if not isinstance(include_group, str):
 258 │                         msg = (
 259 │                             "Dependency group include-group value is not a string: "
 260 │                             f"{item!r}"
 261 │                         )
 262 │                         errors.error(TypeError(msg))
 263 │                     else:
 264 │                         elements.append(
 265 │                             DependencyGroupInclude(include_group=include_group)
 266 │                         )
 267 │             else:
 268 │                 errors.error(TypeError(f"Invalid dependency group item: {item!r}"))
 269 │ 
 270 │         if errors.errors:
 271 │             return ()
 272 │ 
 273 │         self._parsed_groups[group] = tuple(elements)
 274 │         return self._parsed_groups[group]
 275 │ 
 276 │ 
 277 │ # --------------------
 278 │ # Functional Interface
 279 │ # --------------------
 280 │ 
 281 │ 
 282 │ def resolve_dependency_groups(
 283 │     dependency_groups: Mapping[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]], /, *groups: str
 284 │ ) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 285 │     """
 286 │     Resolve a dependency group to a tuple of requirements, as strings.
 287 │ 
 288 │     :param dependency_groups: the parsed contents of the ``[dependency-groups]`` table
 289 │         from ``pyproject.toml``
 290 │     :param groups: the name of the group(s) to resolve
 291 │ 
 292 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 293 │     """
 294 │     resolver = DependencyGroupResolver(dependency_groups)
 295 │     return tuple(str(r) for group in groups for r in resolver.resolve(group))
 296 │ 
 297 │ 
 298 │ # ----------------
 299 │ # internal helpers
 300 │ # ----------------
 301 │ 
 302 │ 
 303 │ _NORMALIZE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[-_.]+")
 304 │ 
 305 │ 
 306 │ def _normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
 307 │     return _NORMALIZE_PATTERN.sub("-", name).lower()
 308 │ 
 309 │ 
 310 │ def _normalize_group_names(
 311 │     dependency_groups: Mapping[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]],
 312 │     errors: _ErrorCollector,
 313 │ ) -> dict[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]]:
 314 │     original_names: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
 315 │     normalized_groups: dict[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]] = {}
 316 │ 
 317 │     for group_name, value in dependency_groups.items():
 318 │         normed_group_name = _normalize_name(group_name)
 319 │         original_names.setdefault(normed_group_name, []).append(group_name)
 320 │         normalized_groups[normed_group_name] = value
 321 │ 
 322 │     for normed_name, names in original_names.items():
 323 │         if len(names) > 1:
 324 │             errors.error(
 325 │                 DuplicateGroupNames(
 326 │                     "Duplicate dependency group names: "
 327 │                     f"{normed_name} ({', '.join(names)})"
 328 │                 )
 329 │             )
 330 │ 
 331 │     return normalized_groups

## Summary

The ticket: exceptions with extra constructor arguments couldn't survive pickling, because the default `__reduce__` reconstructs via `cls(*self.args)`, and these classes only store the message in `args`. I added explicit `__reduce__` methods so the relevant details are preserved.

**Changes:**

- `src/packaging/dependency_groups.py` — `CyclicDependencyGroup.__reduce__` returns `(self.__class__, (requested_group, group, include_group))`, so the three group names round-trip and the message is regenerated identically.
- `src/packaging/metadata.py` — `InvalidMetadata.__reduce__` returns `(self.__class__, (self.field, self.args[0]))`, preserving the field name and message.

**Verification:**

- Targeted tests after the fix: `2 passed in 0.40s` (previously both failed with `TypeError: ... missing required positional argument`).
- Full suite: `python -m pytest -q` → `62105 passed, 417 deselected in 104.25s`.
